5
The diameter of a cylindrical metal rod is measured using a micrometer screw gauge.
The diagram below shows an enlargement of the scale on the micrometer screw gauge when
taking the measurement.
40
3
2
0.5 mm / rev
30
What is the cross-sectional area of the rod?
A
3.81 mm2
B
11.4 mm2
C
22.8 mm2
D
45.6 mm2

hints: Look at the sleeve scale marked $0.5\text{ mm/rev}$: the $3\text{ mm}$ mark plus one extra $0.5\text{ mm}$ mark are past the thimble edge.
Read the thimble where its scale meets the sleeve datum line near $30$: about $31$ divisions of $0.01\text{ mm}$ gives $0.31\text{ mm}$ to add to $3.50\text{ mm}$.
After finding diameter $d$ in $\text{mm}$, compare radius $d/2$ with $d$ before using $A = \pi r^2 = \pi d^2/4$.
walkthrough: Read the main sleeve scale. The $2\text{ mm}$ and $3\text{ mm}$ marks are visible, plus one small $0.5\text{ mm}$ mark after $3\text{ mm}$, so the sleeve contribution is $3.00 + 0.50 = 3.50\text{ mm}$.

Read the thimble scale. One revolution is $0.5\text{ mm}$ and there are $50$ thimble divisions, so each division is $0.01\text{ mm}$. The datum aligns just past $30$, at $31$, giving $31 \times 0.01 = 0.31\text{ mm}$.
Add the parts for the diameter: $d = 3.50 + 0.31 = 3.81\text{ mm}$.
Use the circle area with radius $r = d/2$: $r = 3.81/2 = 1.905\text{ mm}$ and $A = \pi r^2 = \pi \times (1.905)^2$.
Calculate $A \approx \pi \times 3.629 \approx 11.4\text{ mm}^2$ with unit $\text{mm}^2$. This is option B.

A.explanation: This is $3.81$ with units of $\text{mm}^2$. The number $3.81\text{ mm}$ is the measured diameter, not the calculated $\pi d^2/4$.

B.explanation: This is $\pi \times (3.81/2)^2 \approx 11.4\text{ mm}^2$, the correct area from diameter $3.81\text{ mm}$.

C.explanation: This is about twice $11.4\text{ mm}^2$. It follows from mishandling the factor of $4$ when converting diameter to radius in $A = \pi d^2/4$.

D.explanation: This is $\pi \times (3.81)^2 \approx 45.6\text{ mm}^2$. It uses the full diameter $3.81\text{ mm}$ as if it were the radius.
